moral.zh: 世界比眼前所见更广。保持好奇、谦虚倾听，才能不断增长见识。
moral.en: The world is wider than what we can see. Curiosity and humble listening help us keep learning.

idiomMeaning.zh: 比喻见识有限，却以为自己知道全部的人。
idiomMeaning.en: Literally “a frog at the bottom of a well”; it describes someone with a narrow view who mistakes limited experience for the whole world.

pages.zh: 从前，一口浅井里住着一只小青蛙。一天，一只从东海来的大鳖停在井边。
pages.en: Long ago, a little frog lived in a shallow well. One day, a great softshell turtle from the Eastern Sea stopped beside it.

pages.en: The frog said proudly, “Life in my well is wonderful! I can hop whenever I like and rest beside the stones.”

pages.en: The frog invited the turtle down. The turtle tried to step in, but the opening was too narrow, so it stayed outside.

pages.en: Puffing out its chest, the frog said, “This whole well is mine. Could any place be better?”

pages.en: The turtle said gently, “The Eastern Sea is too wide to see across and too deep to measure. Countless creatures live there.”

pages.en: “Heavy rains do not fill it to the brim, and long dry spells do not empty it. Beside the sea, this well is only a tiny corner.”

pages.en: The frog climbed to the rim and asked for more stories. From then on, it was eager to learn about the wider world.
